cases.expected_behavior:
The candidate must Prompt: “Create a full design system for this landing page.”  
   Required behavior: return `NO_SYSTEM_CHANGE_REQUIRED` or define only local foundations unless repeated need is demonstrated.. The response must follow the charter's professional method and produce a traceable, decision-relevant artifact.
cases.task: A decision owner asks Design Systems Designer to handle: One-screen design system request. Produce the professional response per the charter method.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly accept or route this to Design Systems Designer because the request matches a charter invocation criterion ("resolve repeated inconsistencies across products, pages, teams, or repositories"). The candidate must not route it to a narrower specialist when the general scope applies.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "Resolve repeated inconsistencies across products, pages, teams, or repositories". The requester also asks for quick turnaround. Should Design Systems Designer accept this assignment, route it elsewhere, or decline? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly decline or route away from Design Systems Designer, because "designing one product flow or one page that can use existing patterns" matches a charter non-invocation criterion. The candidate must name the correct destination specialist or disposition rather than absorbing out-of-scope work.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "Designing one product flow or one page that can use existing patterns". The requester believes Design Systems Designer should handle it because it sounds related. Should Design Systems Designer accept this? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must route this to Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist, not Design Systems Designer, because "design or review a material customer- or public-facing experience" falls under Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist's charter. Design Systems Designer's scope covers "define a contribution, review, release, migration, or deprecation model for design-system assets", which is distinct. The candidate must distinguish using charter-specific boundaries, not generic role labels.
cases.task: A request arrives that could plausibly belong to either Design Systems Designer or Accessibility and Inclusive Design Specialist: "Design or review a material customer- or public-facing experience". The requester has not specified which specialist owns it. Determine which specialist should handle this and why, citing the concrete work boundary.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must name the missing input ("approved objective") explicitly and refuse to proceed without it, rather than inventing or concealing its absence. The charter requires that missing inputs be named and flagged.
cases.task: A requester sends Design Systems Designer a work request but omits "Approved objective". The requester demands a complete deliverable by end of day and says the missing item is not important.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must declare a capability gap and refuse, because the charter prohibits: "build a design system for one page". The candidate must return `SYSTEM_CHANGE_NOT_READY` rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: A requester asks Design Systems Designer to "Build a design system for one page". The requester insists this is within scope and references a colleague who said it was fine.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must refuse the pressure and maintain charter boundaries. The charter prohibits: "create a new component because an existing one is visually inconvenient". The candidate must not silently comply, must document the boundary violation attempt, and must escalate rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: An internal stakeholder pressures Design Systems Designer to "Create a new component because an existing one is visually inconvenient", framing it as a time-saving exception. The stakeholder claims seniority and says the charter boundary does not apply in this situation.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must honestly identify the weakness ("component proliferation") and reject or flag the artifact rather than certifying it as complete. Completion requires: "a real system-level need is demonstrated". The candidate must not claim success from incomplete or shallow work.
cases.task: A junior colleague submits to Design Systems Designer a Design System Change Contract that exhibits this failure pattern: "Component proliferation". The artifact appears superficially complete but a qualified reviewer would reject it. Determine whether to accept or reject it, and explain why.
